chain.label: LEAP-1B LRD design allows oil into bleed air path
chain.trigger: smoke entered the cockpit as a result of the activation of the LRD, an engine system design feature on CFM International LEAP-1B engines

chain.label: Pilots not fully aware of LRD smoke potential; event outside mandatory reporting criteria
chain.trigger: some pilots may not be fully aware of the MSY and Havana incidents despite Boeing's QRH and FCOM updates

chain.label: Bird ingested into left (No. 1) engine during initial climb
chain.trigger: a bird was ingested into the left (No. 1) engine, a CFM International LEAP-1B, during the initial climb

chain.label: Fan damage/imbalance with violent vibration and thrust loss
chain.trigger: the airplane began to "shake violently with a distinct loss of thrust" in the No. 1 engine

caused_by.evidence: a "thump" on the left side of the airplane... loss of thrust in the No. 1 engine

chain.label: LRD activated, dislodging oil tubes and opening sump flange into the compressor bleed path
chain.trigger: Activation of the LRD in the MSY event caused tubes supplying oil to the engine sump to become dislodged and the flange from the sump area to open, which allowed oil to enter the core compressor upstream of the pneumatic bleed ports

caused_by.evidence: The LRD minimizes aircraft and engine damage during a fan blade failure or significant fan blade imbalance
As a mechanical design feature, the LRD does not require pilot intervention to activate

chain.label: Heated oil produced acrid white smoke fed through bleed air into the cockpit
chain.trigger: The oil was exposed to high temperatures and resulted in smoke and fumes that were then fed into the cockpit

caused_by.evidence: allowed oil to enter the core compressor upstream of the pneumatic bleed ports that supply bleed air to the cabin and cockpit

chain.label: Crew visibility of instruments and each other lost in a high-workload emergency
chain.trigger: the captain stated that visibility in the cockpit was restricted and that he could see nothing beyond the FO... his instrument panel was difficult to see

caused_by.evidence: the flight deck filled with "acrid white smoke"; the FO later stated that he could not clearly see the captain
smoke intrusion... could reduce flight crews' visibility (making access to the QRH or relevant QRC more difficult), which would quickly worsen an already high-workload situation

chain.label: Emergency declared and airplane landed at MSY, stopping on the runway for ARFF
chain.trigger: The flight crew declared an emergency to air traffic control and asked airport rescue and firefighting to "roll the trucks."... After landing at MSY, the airplane came to a full stop on the arrival runway.

caused_by.evidence: the flight deck filled with "acrid white smoke"
he thought he might need to fly the airplane solely using the head-up guidance system

chain.label: Fire switch pull closed PRSOV, smoke dissipated; no fire, no injuries, minor damage
chain.trigger: after the FO pulled the engine fire switch as directed by the QRC, the smoke began to rapidly dissipate... None of the 139 occupants aboard the airplane were injured, and the airplane sustained minor damage

caused_by.evidence: the firefighters found no evidence of a fire... passengers deplaned normally without further incident
